**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

### OFK Grbalj in European competitions

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: OFK Grbalj in European competitions")]

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

### OFK Grbalj in European competitions

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: OFK Grbalj in European competitions")]

For the first time, OFK Grbalj played in European competitions on season [2007-08](/wiki/2007_UEFA_Intertoto_Cup "2007 UEFA Intertoto Cup").

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

### OFK Grbalj in European competitions

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: OFK Grbalj in European competitions")]

For the first time, OFK Grbalj played in European competitions on season [2007-08](/wiki/2007_UEFA_Intertoto_Cup "2007 UEFA Intertoto Cup").  
They were first team from Montenegrin coastal region which played in [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") competitions. Until now, OFK Grbalj played two seasons in European cups.

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

\"Serbian Cyrillic alphabet\"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian \"Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian\")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro \"Montenegro\") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football \"Association football\") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\").\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 \"Edit section: History\")]\\n\\nThe first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League \"Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)\") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia \"FR Yugoslavia\") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia \"1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia\"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  \\nAfter [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 \"Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006\"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League \"Montenegrin First League\"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta \"FK Zeta\") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica \"FK Budućnost Podgorica\"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn\\'t achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  \\nOFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom \"FK Kom\") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar \"FK Mornar\") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro \"Bar, Montenegro\") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  \\nIn the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup \"2016–17 Montenegrin Cup\"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 \"FK Sutjeska Nikšić\") 1–0.  \\nAfter 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League \"2019-20 Montenegrin First League\"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\").\\n\\n### First League Record\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=2 \"Edit section: First League Record\")]\\n\\nSee also: [Participants of Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League#All_time_tables \"Montenegrin First League\")\\n\\nFor the first time, OFK Grbalj played in Montenegrin First League on season [2006–07](/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_Montenegrin_First_League \"2006–07 Montenegrin First League\"). **Radanovići** ([Montenegrin Cyrillic](/wiki/Montenegrin_Cyrillic "Montenegrin Cyrillic"): Радановићи) is a small town in the [municipality](/wiki/Municipalities_of_Montenegro "Municipalities of Montenegro") of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor_Municipality "Kotor Municipality"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"). The town is also part and largest settlement of historical rural region of [Grbalj](/wiki/Grbalj "Grbalj") at the [coastal region of Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegrin_littoral "Montenegrin littoral"). The town of Radanovići is located near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and the [Bay of Kotor](/wiki/Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor") region.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Demographics
------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Demographics")]

The settlement has a population of 752 inhabitants, according 2011 census, and is mainly populated by [Serbs](/wiki/Serbs_of_Montenegro "Serbs of Montenegro") (63.69%), with a significant population of [Montenegrins](/wiki/Montenegrins "Montenegrins") (21.14%)[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Transport
---------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Transport")]

The town of Radanovići is situated approximately halfway between two main Montenegrin tourist destinations, [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"), on the main road that connects these two. [Tivat Airport](/wiki/Tivat_Airport "Tivat Airport") is 7.5 km (4.6 mi) away, and there are regular flights to [Belgrade](/wiki/Belgrade "Belgrade") throughout the year, and dozens of charter planes land daily at the airport during the summer season.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Sports
------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Sports")]

Local football team [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj") play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara") and currently compete in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League").

**Stadion Donja Sutvara** is a football [stadium](/wiki/Stadium "Stadium") in Radanovići, [Municipality of Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"). It is used for [football](/wiki/Football_(soccer) "Football (soccer)") matches and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj"). The stadium holds 1,500 people.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stadion_Donja_Sutvara&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The stadium was built in 1995 near the village Donja Sutvara, on the outskirts of Radanovići. It is situated near the main road between [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor") and [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj").  
In 2004, Donja Sutvara stadium was renovated to meet the criteria for games in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). The stadium consists of one level with a capacity of 1,500 seats.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Pitch and conditions
--------------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stadion_Donja_Sutvara&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Pitch and conditions")]

The pitch measures 110 x 65 meters. The stadium didn't met [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") criteria for European competitions.

**Stadion Donja Sutvara** is a football [stadium](/wiki/Stadium "Stadium") in Radanovići, [Municipality of Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"). It is used for [football](/wiki/Football_(soccer) "Football (soccer)") matches and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj"). The stadium holds 1,500 people.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stadion_Donja_Sutvara&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The stadium was built in 1995 near the village Donja Sutvara, on the outskirts of Radanovići. It is situated near the main road between [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor") and [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj").  
In 2004, Donja Sutvara stadium was renovated to meet the criteria for games in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). The stadium consists of one level with a capacity of 1,500 seats.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Pitch and conditions
--------------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stadion_Donja_Sutvara&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Pitch and conditions")]

The pitch measures 110 x 65 meters. The stadium didn't met [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") criteria for European competitions.

**Radanovići** ([Montenegrin Cyrillic](/wiki/Montenegrin_Cyrillic "Montenegrin Cyrillic"): Радановићи) is a small town in the [municipality](/wiki/Municipalities_of_Montenegro "Municipalities of Montenegro") of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor_Municipality "Kotor Municipality"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"). The town is also part and largest settlement of historical rural region of [Grbalj](/wiki/Grbalj "Grbalj") at the [coastal region of Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegrin_littoral "Montenegrin littoral"). The town of Radanovići is located near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and the [Bay of Kotor](/wiki/Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor") region.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Demographics
------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Demographics")]

The settlement has a population of 752 inhabitants, according 2011 census, and is mainly populated by [Serbs](/wiki/Serbs_of_Montenegro "Serbs of Montenegro") (63.69%), with a significant population of [Montenegrins](/wiki/Montenegrins "Montenegrins") (21.14%)[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Transport
---------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Transport")]

The town of Radanovići is situated approximately halfway between two main Montenegrin tourist destinations, [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"), on the main road that connects these two. [Tivat Airport](/wiki/Tivat_Airport "Tivat Airport") is 7.5 km (4.6 mi) away, and there are regular flights to [Belgrade](/wiki/Belgrade "Belgrade") throughout the year, and dozens of charter planes land daily at the airport during the summer season.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Sports
------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Sports")]

Local football team [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj") play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara") and currently compete in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League").

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

### OFK Grbalj in European competitions

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: OFK Grbalj in European competitions")]

For the first time, OFK Grbalj played in European competitions on season [2007-08](/wiki/2007_UEFA_Intertoto_Cup "2007 UEFA Intertoto Cup").

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Stadion Donja Sutvara** is a football [stadium](/wiki/Stadium "Stadium") in Radanovići, [Municipality of Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"). It is used for [football](/wiki/Football_(soccer) "Football (soccer)") matches and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj"). The stadium holds 1,500 people.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stadion_Donja_Sutvara&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The stadium was built in 1995 near the village Donja Sutvara, on the outskirts of Radanovići. It is situated near the main road between [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor") and [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj").  
In 2004, Donja Sutvara stadium was renovated to meet the criteria for games in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). The stadium consists of one level with a capacity of 1,500 seats.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Pitch and conditions
--------------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stadion_Donja_Sutvara&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Pitch and conditions")]

The pitch measures 110 x 65 meters. The stadium didn't met [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") criteria for European competitions.

**Radanovići** ([Montenegrin Cyrillic](/wiki/Montenegrin_Cyrillic "Montenegrin Cyrillic"): Радановићи) is a small town in the [municipality](/wiki/Municipalities_of_Montenegro "Municipalities of Montenegro") of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor_Municipality "Kotor Municipality"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"). The town is also part and largest settlement of historical rural region of [Grbalj](/wiki/Grbalj "Grbalj") at the [coastal region of Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegrin_littoral "Montenegrin littoral"). The town of Radanovići is located near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and the [Bay of Kotor](/wiki/Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor") region.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Demographics
------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Demographics")]

The settlement has a population of 752 inhabitants, according 2011 census, and is mainly populated by [Serbs](/wiki/Serbs_of_Montenegro "Serbs of Montenegro") (63.69%), with a significant population of [Montenegrins](/wiki/Montenegrins "Montenegrins") (21.14%)[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Transport
---------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Transport")]

The town of Radanovići is situated approximately halfway between two main Montenegrin tourist destinations, [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"), on the main road that connects these two. [Tivat Airport](/wiki/Tivat_Airport "Tivat Airport") is 7.5 km (4.6 mi) away, and there are regular flights to [Belgrade](/wiki/Belgrade "Belgrade") throughout the year, and dozens of charter planes land daily at the airport during the summer season.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Sports
------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Sports")]

Local football team [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj") play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara") and currently compete in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League").

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Stadion Donja Sutvara** is a football [stadium](/wiki/Stadium "Stadium") in Radanovići, [Municipality of Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"). It is used for [football](/wiki/Football_(soccer) "Football (soccer)") matches and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj"). The stadium holds 1,500 people.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stadion_Donja_Sutvara&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The stadium was built in 1995 near the village Donja Sutvara, on the outskirts of Radanovići. It is situated near the main road between [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor") and [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj").  
In 2004, Donja Sutvara stadium was renovated to meet the criteria for games in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). The stadium consists of one level with a capacity of 1,500 seats.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Pitch and conditions
--------------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stadion_Donja_Sutvara&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Pitch and conditions")]

The pitch measures 110 x 65 meters. The stadium didn't met [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") criteria for European competitions.

**Radanovići** ([Montenegrin Cyrillic](/wiki/Montenegrin_Cyrillic "Montenegrin Cyrillic"): Радановићи) is a small town in the [municipality](/wiki/Municipalities_of_Montenegro "Municipalities of Montenegro") of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor_Municipality "Kotor Municipality"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"). The town is also part and largest settlement of historical rural region of [Grbalj](/wiki/Grbalj "Grbalj") at the [coastal region of Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegrin_littoral "Montenegrin littoral"). The town of Radanovići is located near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and the [Bay of Kotor](/wiki/Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor") region.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Demographics
------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Demographics")]

The settlement has a population of 752 inhabitants, according 2011 census, and is mainly populated by [Serbs](/wiki/Serbs_of_Montenegro "Serbs of Montenegro") (63.69%), with a significant population of [Montenegrins](/wiki/Montenegrins "Montenegrins") (21.14%)[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Transport
---------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Transport")]

The town of Radanovići is situated approximately halfway between two main Montenegrin tourist destinations, [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"), on the main road that connects these two. [Tivat Airport](/wiki/Tivat_Airport "Tivat Airport") is 7.5 km (4.6 mi) away, and there are regular flights to [Belgrade](/wiki/Belgrade "Belgrade") throughout the year, and dozens of charter planes land daily at the airport during the summer season.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Sports
------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Sports")]

Local football team [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj") play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara") and currently compete in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League").

\"Serbian Cyrillic alphabet\"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian \"Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian\")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro \"Montenegro\") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football \"Association football\") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\").\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 \"Edit section: History\")]\\n\\nThe first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League \"Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)\") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia \"FR Yugoslavia\") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia \"1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia\"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  \\nAfter [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 \"Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006\"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League \"Montenegrin First League\"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta \"FK Zeta\") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica \"FK Budućnost Podgorica\"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn\\'t achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  \\nOFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom \"FK Kom\") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar \"FK Mornar\") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro \"Bar, Montenegro\") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  \\nIn the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup \"2016–17 Montenegrin Cup\"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 \"FK Sutjeska Nikšić\") 1–0.  \\nAfter 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League \"2019-20 Montenegrin First League\"). It is used for [football](/wiki/Football_(soccer) \"Football (soccer)\") matches and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj \"OFK Grbalj\"). The stadium holds 1,500 people.\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stadion_Donja_Sutvara&action=edit&section=1 \"Edit section: History\")]\\n\\nThe stadium was built in 1995 near the village Donja Sutvara, on the outskirts of Radanovići. It is situated near the main road between [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor \"Kotor\") and [Budva](/wiki/Budva \"Budva\") and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj \"OFK Grbalj\").  \\nIn 2004, Donja Sutvara stadium was renovated to meet the criteria for games in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League \"Montenegrin First League\"). The town of Radanovići is located near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva \"Budva\") and the [Bay of Kotor](/wiki/Bay_of_Kotor \"Bay of Kotor\") region.[[1]](#cite_note-1)\\n\\nDemographics\\n------------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=1 \"Edit section: Demographics\")]\\n\\nThe settlement has a population of 752 inhabitants, according 2011 census, and is mainly populated by [Serbs](/wiki/Serbs_of_Montenegro \"Serbs of Montenegro\") (63.69%), with a significant population of [Montenegrins](/wiki/Montenegrins \"Montenegrins\") (21.14%)[[2]](#cite_note-2)\\n\\nTransport\\n---------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=2 \"Edit section: Transport\")]\\n\\nThe town of Radanovići is situated approximately halfway between two main Montenegrin tourist destinations, [Budva](/wiki/Budva \"Budva\") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor \"Kotor\"), on the main road that connects these two. **Luca Banti** (Italian: [[ˈluːka ˈbanti]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); born 27 March 1974 in [Livorno](/wiki/Livorno "Livorno"))[[1]](#cite_note-1) is an [Italian](/wiki/Italians "Italians") [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") [referee](/wiki/Referee_(association_football) "Referee (association football)"). In 2009, he became a UEFA Category three referee and at the start of 2010 he was promoted to category two and later to category one.

Banti became a [FIFA](/wiki/FIFA_International_Referees_List "FIFA International Referees List") referee in 2009.[[2]](#cite_note-2) He has served as a referee in [2014 World Cup qualifiers](/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_(UEFA) "2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)").[[3]](#cite_note-3)

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Stadion Donja Sutvara** is a football [stadium](/wiki/Stadium "Stadium") in Radanovići, [Municipality of Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"). It is used for [football](/wiki/Football_(soccer) "Football (soccer)") matches and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj"). The stadium holds 1,500 people.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stadion_Donja_Sutvara&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The stadium was built in 1995 near the village Donja Sutvara, on the outskirts of Radanovići. It is situated near the main road between [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor") and [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj").  
In 2004, Donja Sutvara stadium was renovated to meet the criteria for games in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). The stadium consists of one level with a capacity of 1,500 seats.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Pitch and conditions
--------------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stadion_Donja_Sutvara&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Pitch and conditions")]

The pitch measures 110 x 65 meters. The stadium didn't met [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") criteria for European competitions.

**Radanovići** ([Montenegrin Cyrillic](/wiki/Montenegrin_Cyrillic "Montenegrin Cyrillic"): Радановићи) is a small town in the [municipality](/wiki/Municipalities_of_Montenegro "Municipalities of Montenegro") of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor_Municipality "Kotor Municipality"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"). The town is also part and largest settlement of historical rural region of [Grbalj](/wiki/Grbalj "Grbalj") at the [coastal region of Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegrin_littoral "Montenegrin littoral"). The town of Radanovići is located near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and the [Bay of Kotor](/wiki/Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor") region.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Demographics
------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Demographics")]

The settlement has a population of 752 inhabitants, according 2011 census, and is mainly populated by [Serbs](/wiki/Serbs_of_Montenegro "Serbs of Montenegro") (63.69%), with a significant population of [Montenegrins](/wiki/Montenegrins "Montenegrins") (21.14%)[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Transport
---------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Transport")]

The town of Radanovići is situated approximately halfway between two main Montenegrin tourist destinations, [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"), on the main road that connects these two. [Tivat Airport](/wiki/Tivat_Airport "Tivat Airport") is 7.5 km (4.6 mi) away, and there are regular flights to [Belgrade](/wiki/Belgrade "Belgrade") throughout the year, and dozens of charter planes land daily at the airport during the summer season.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Sports
------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Sports")]

Local football team [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj") play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara") and currently compete in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League").

**Luca Banti** (Italian: [[ˈluːka ˈbanti]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); born 27 March 1974 in [Livorno](/wiki/Livorno "Livorno"))[[1]](#cite_note-1) is an [Italian](/wiki/Italians "Italians") [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") [referee](/wiki/Referee_(association_football) "Referee (association football)"). In 2009, he became a UEFA Category three referee and at the start of 2010 he was promoted to category two and later to category one.

Banti became a [FIFA](/wiki/FIFA_International_Referees_List "FIFA International Referees List") referee in 2009.[[2]](#cite_note-2) He has served as a referee in [2014 World Cup qualifiers](/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_(UEFA) "2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)").[[3]](#cite_note-3)

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

### OFK Grbalj in European competitions

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: OFK Grbalj in European competitions")]

For the first time, OFK Grbalj played in European competitions on season [2007-08](/wiki/2007_UEFA_Intertoto_Cup "2007 UEFA Intertoto Cup").

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Stadion Donja Sutvara** is a football [stadium](/wiki/Stadium "Stadium") in Radanovići, [Municipality of Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"). It is used for [football](/wiki/Football_(soccer) "Football (soccer)") matches and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj"). The stadium holds 1,500 people.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stadion_Donja_Sutvara&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The stadium was built in 1995 near the village Donja Sutvara, on the outskirts of Radanovići. It is situated near the main road between [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor") and [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj").  
In 2004, Donja Sutvara stadium was renovated to meet the criteria for games in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). The stadium consists of one level with a capacity of 1,500 seats.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Pitch and conditions
--------------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stadion_Donja_Sutvara&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Pitch and conditions")]

The pitch measures 110 x 65 meters. The stadium didn't met [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") criteria for European competitions.

**Radanovići** ([Montenegrin Cyrillic](/wiki/Montenegrin_Cyrillic "Montenegrin Cyrillic"): Радановићи) is a small town in the [municipality](/wiki/Municipalities_of_Montenegro "Municipalities of Montenegro") of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor_Municipality "Kotor Municipality"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"). The town is also part and largest settlement of historical rural region of [Grbalj](/wiki/Grbalj "Grbalj") at the [coastal region of Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegrin_littoral "Montenegrin littoral"). The town of Radanovići is located near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and the [Bay of Kotor](/wiki/Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor") region.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

Demographics
------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Demographics")]

The settlement has a population of 752 inhabitants, according 2011 census, and is mainly populated by [Serbs](/wiki/Serbs_of_Montenegro "Serbs of Montenegro") (63.69%), with a significant population of [Montenegrins](/wiki/Montenegrins "Montenegrins") (21.14%)[[2]](#cite_note-2)

Transport
---------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Transport")]

The town of Radanovići is situated approximately halfway between two main Montenegrin tourist destinations, [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"), on the main road that connects these two. [Tivat Airport](/wiki/Tivat_Airport "Tivat Airport") is 7.5 km (4.6 mi) away, and there are regular flights to [Belgrade](/wiki/Belgrade "Belgrade") throughout the year, and dozens of charter planes land daily at the airport during the summer season.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Sports
------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Sports")]

Local football team [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj") play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara") and currently compete in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League").

**Luca Banti** (Italian: [[ˈluːka ˈbanti]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian"); born 27 March 1974 in [Livorno](/wiki/Livorno "Livorno"))[[1]](#cite_note-1) is an [Italian](/wiki/Italians "Italians") [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") [referee](/wiki/Referee_(association_football) "Referee (association football)"). In 2009, he became a UEFA Category three referee and at the start of 2010 he was promoted to category two and later to category one.

Banti became a [FIFA](/wiki/FIFA_International_Referees_List "FIFA International Referees List") referee in 2009.[[2]](#cite_note-2) He has served as a referee in [2014 World Cup qualifiers](/wiki/2014_FIFA_World_Cup_qualification_(UEFA) "2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)").[[3]](#cite_note-3)

[Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro \"Montenegro\") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football \"Association football\") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\").\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 \"Edit section: History\")]\\n\\nThe first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League \"Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)\") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia \"FR Yugoslavia\") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia \"1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia\"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  \\nAfter [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 \"Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006\"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League \"Montenegrin First League\"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta \"FK Zeta\") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica \"FK Budućnost Podgorica\"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn\\'t achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  \\nOFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom \"FK Kom\") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar \"FK Mornar\") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro \"Bar, Montenegro\") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  \\nIn the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup \"2016–17 Montenegrin Cup\"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 \"FK Sutjeska Nikšić\") 1–0.  \\nAfter 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League \"2019-20 Montenegrin First League\"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\").\\n\\n### First League Record\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=2 \"Edit section: First League Record\")]\\n\\nSee also: [Participants of Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League#All_time_tables \"Montenegrin First League\")\\n\\nFor the first time, OFK Grbalj played in Montenegrin First League on season [2006–07](/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_Montenegrin_First_League \"2006–07 Montenegrin First League\"). It is used for [football](/wiki/Football_(soccer) \"Football (soccer)\") matches and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj \"OFK Grbalj\"). The stadium holds 1,500 people.\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Stadion_Donja_Sutvara&action=edit&section=1 \"Edit section: History\")]\\n\\nThe stadium was built in 1995 near the village Donja Sutvara, on the outskirts of Radanovići. It is situated near the main road between [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor \"Kotor\") and [Budva](/wiki/Budva \"Budva\") and is the home turf of [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj \"OFK Grbalj\").  \\nIn 2004, Donja Sutvara stadium was renovated to meet the criteria for games in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League \"Montenegrin First League\"). **Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

### OFK Grbalj in European competitions

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: OFK Grbalj in European competitions")]

For the first time, OFK Grbalj played in European competitions on season [2007-08](/wiki/2007_UEFA_Intertoto_Cup "2007 UEFA Intertoto Cup").  
They were first team from Montenegrin coastal region which played in [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") competitions. Until now, OFK Grbalj played two seasons in European cups.

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

### OFK Grbalj in European competitions

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: OFK Grbalj in European competitions")]

For the first time, OFK Grbalj played in European competitions on season [2007-08](/wiki/2007_UEFA_Intertoto_Cup "2007 UEFA Intertoto Cup").  
They were first team from Montenegrin coastal region which played in [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") competitions. Until now, OFK Grbalj played two seasons in European cups.

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.
